newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bremen cotton buyers look for nearby cover.
newsitem.headline: Bremen cotton buyers look for nearby cover.

text.p: German and some other western European yarn spinners were seeking cotton for near-term shipment, a fortnightly market report from the Bremen Cotton Exchange said on Monday.
It said the buyers were trying to offset dollar-induced higher mark prices by requesting lower differentials.
Although they were mostly unsuccessful, they accepted upland cotton offers from Central Asian and West African shippers, with trades reported for dates throughout 1997.
Sales in Indian medium and high grades developed for Feb-June and Iranian middling cotton sold for March/April.

In the longstaple sector, the Exchange reported trades in Egyptian Giza 77 and 75/86 and Sudan-Barakat for the second quarter, Israel-Pima for second and third and U.S.-Pima for the fourth quarter 1997 and first quarter 1998.
Cotton stocks as of Feb 21 totalled 34,742 bales, little changed from a fortnight earlier, but well below 121,625 recorded a year earlier.
